# VDOM settlement exceptions strand late update work

## Context

An operator-requested post-merge challenge of #19468 reproduced an exception-path regression with real Container/Component instances and the standard single-thread VDOM setup.

Compared pre-PR `6e19f6031b3d7625f16197c7b8064fed0e07083a` with head `08f43d63b2c88c58c7a469804b21edc82e663bf9`. The merged `fb11d56b24756d76f26dc6dcb8c6f8408927128d` lifecycle blob is identical (`763e8ab9948c1a01b2dc58d2423ae39d3a1d9a7d`). This is an injected callback-failure witness, not a claim of an observed user-facing Grid outage.

## The Problem

Hold a real `Helper.updateBatch` response, queue a later `promiseUpdate()` and VDOM change on its root, register a throwing `VDomUpdate.registerPreUpdate()` callback, then release the response.

| Observed after all started executions settle | Before | Merged head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Late promise | rejected | still pending |
| Update flights | 2 | 1 |
| Queued VDOM class rendered | yes | no |
| `needsVdomUpdate` / parked callbacks | false / false | true / true |

A second control with a throwing claimed resolver leaves an in-flight registry entry on the merged head; the baseline clears it and performs the queued render. The callback failure must remain visible, but it must not strand unrelated queued work.

Design authority: `VdomLifecycle.promiseUpdate()` documents rejection of parked promises on a failing flight, including late requests. `resolveVdomUpdate()` and the existing catch own release and subsequent queued updates.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:459` deletes the root from `inFlightScopes` before calling `resolveVdomUpdate()`.
- Settlement invokes callbacks, unregisters the flight, releases post-updates and runs `executePreUpdates()` before starting queued work.
- A synchronous throw returns to the catch with that root already absent, so its rejection/retry cleanup is skipped.
- `src/grid/Body.mjs#createViewData` is an existing production consumer of `registerPreUpdate()`; the diagnostic injects a failure at that consumed hook.
- `VDomUpdate.executePreUpdates()` already removes its hook before invocation. This is not an infinitely recurring test callback.
- Owning regression location: `test/playwright/unit/vdom/VdomLifecycle.spec.mjs`.

## The Fix

Make per-root settlement exception-safe in the owning lifecycle. Retire a root's cleanup responsibility only when its settlement has completed or its failure has been handled. Preserve instance/cycle identity checks so old cleanup cannot unregister a replacement or a newer flight started reentrantly. Keep all-root vnode adoption before callbacks and the new emitted-root protection.

Do not swallow callback exceptions, acknowledge an unrendered payload, broadly reject another root's successful work, or restore initiator-only protection.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Authority | Required behavior | Failure | Documentation | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Root settlement | `resolveVdomUpdate` and batch catch | Correct flight ownership remains until settlement/cleanup finishes | Throwing hook/resolver leaves no orphaned registry or late promise | Owning lifecycle JSDoc | Held-response callback-failure controls |
| Late `promiseUpdate()` | Existing method JSDoc | Retain next-flight success semantics; reject honestly on covered failure | Pending work cannot silently strand | Existing promise contract | Late mutation plus promise, baseline/head comparison |
| Reentrant/replaced root | Existing instance/cycle fences | Preserve a new instance or newer flight | Stale cleanup cannot clear it | Existing ownership comments | Reentry, destruction and reused-ID controls |
| Captured completion phases | Existing pre-/post-update queues | `executePreUpdates(id, callback?)` and `triggerPostUpdates(ownerId, item?)` run explicitly supplied detached snapshots; one-argument calls consume live entries; explicit null/undefined consumes none | Newer hooks/queues survive, including reuse of the same callback function | Both methods and lifecycle JSDoc | Reentrant old/new phase controls and legacy one-argument controls |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic regression reproduces the throwing pre-update case on `08f43d63`, then shows the late promise settles under the existing failure contract and queued rendering can proceed.
- [ ] A throwing settlement resolver cannot leave a stale in-flight registry/watchdog entry or silently strand queued work.
- [ ] Mixed-root success, rejection, late requests, destruction/replacement and reentrant starts retain their ownership and settlement guarantees.
- [ ] Sparse payloads and emitted-root collision protection remain intact; focused lifecycle tests pass.

## Out of Scope

Changing asymmetric batching, refining scalar-depth collision coverage, Main-thread DOM deduplication, and claiming an installed FM or whole-release acceptance result. The earlier `afterSetMounted` callback failure that occurs before common settlement is independently tracked in #19478; the initialization control here covers the shared `resolveVdomUpdate` pre-hook path.

Decision Record impact: none; restores the existing exception/settlement contract. Structure map: N/A, existing Body lifecycle and spec, no new production module.

Related: #19467, #19468, #17844.

Ownership: Sophie implements this operator-prioritized stability repair. Keep batching/collision protection intact; hot-path optimization is a separate follow-up.

- The original paired diagnostic now rejects the late pre-update promise, renders its queued state and clears resolver-failure registry entries while retaining the asymmetric payload shapes and collision protection.
- One fresh real-browser guard ran all six prior workloads on this commit. DOM/vnode/App final values pass; the 2s/4ms stream accepted 500 inputs, settled 1,000 promises and emitted 121 batches, with 15.3ms final drain. Instrumented App-work medians were 0.4/0.2/1.0/1.5/5.05ms for the two toolbar shapes and 17/65/257 roots. This is a healthy-path guard within the earlier observed ranges, not a new paired performance claim or an optimization certificate.

The earlier mount-resolver failure occurs before common settlement and is tracked independently in #19478; it is unchanged in the exact older-callback control. The initialization regression here covers the later common pre-update-hook path. Installed FM and the large-batch optimization remain separate.
